reviewHtml:
CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Aisling Camps offered a chipper start to the morning with her debut runway show, held at Bortolami Gallery in Tribeca. The designer first joined the official NYFW schedule last season and it’s our hope that she keeps on going. Camps began her brand when she moved home to Trinidad after making a sudden career jump from engineer to knitwear designer. There she explored how knitwear, an untraditional warm weather apparel choice, could be thought of in a totally different manner. One advantage of this Caribbean beginning, she said with a laugh, is that fewer people have encountered her early youthful, “not self-conscious” works, some of which she revisited in today’s show: “I can give these designs new attention with so many more resources—and no one saw it either.”

But plenty of eyes were on Camps’s designs as the models padded down the runway in barely-there jelly flip flops tied up with excess yarn and stacked with plenty of toe rings. It’s probably the most beachy a concrete gallery floor has felt. “It was just really fun to return to my beach girl days, you know I’m definitely the girl pumping gas in a bikini,” she said, unable to resist including items like a black crochet coverup dress and a handful of knit bikini briefs. Brooklyn Bridge Park or the Caribbean coast? You decide.

Devotees of the brand will recognize a few familiar shapes from last season, including triangle bra tops and a sheer top-cum-dress, in the faintest of mints, that can be tied up or let down depending on the mood. Off the shoulder cardigans offered buildable options that could be mixed in or out of many of the looks. There’s a fluidity to Camps’s approach, continually bringing pieces from past seasons forward to the next to gradually establish a “core collection.”

Everything in the Aisling Camps universe is measured—it has to be, hand knitting is a precise science, expressed this season in a succinct 20 looks—yet the loose knits sloping off the shoulders and fringed criss-crossed tank tops (another design from her early days) were wonderfully carefree. A bit of an outlier in comparison, but a crowd favorite: a “distressed prep” rugby shirt inspired by her collegiate days as an undergraduate at Columbia. New Englanders should take Camps’s advice and swap the salmon chinos for an asymmetrical mini. Meanwhile, a personal highlight was a tie between the skirt’s second appearance, this time paired with a netted white cardigan and layered over an ivory slip, and a white geometric sweater vest worn with a fringed short sleeve T-shirt (Camps wore a black version of the vest for her own finale bow). Bravo!
